cases.description: The reference case: a production-mode document, the pinned AWS root, PCR0/1/2/8 from this very enclave, and a now inside the leaf certificate's window. Every check that has inputs passes; the two receipt bindings report not_implemented because this document carries no public_key or user_data.
cases.name: production-enclave-fully-pinned

cases.description: The same document checked years later, the way a receipt is read. max_age_seconds is None, so freshness is not asked; certificate validity is still measured against the moment the document was produced, which is why an old receipt still verifies.
cases.name: production-enclave-no-freshness-bound

cases.description: Nothing pinned. The document is genuine and every cryptographic check passes, and the PCR check still reports not_implemented: a document nobody compared to an expected measurement proves only that some enclave produced it.
cases.name: no-pcr-allowlist-is-not-a-pass

cases.description: The document is untouched; the operator pinned a different image. This is the everyday failure: someone deployed an enclave nobody approved.
cases.name: pcr0-does-not-match-the-allowlist

cases.description: A real, unmodified, correctly signed document verified against a root that is not the AWS Nitro root. The signature still verifies — every document is self-consistent — and the chain check refuses it anyway.
cases.name: chain-does-not-reach-the-pinned-root

cases.description: One hour after the document was produced, with a five-minute bound. The chain and the signature are untouched; only freshness fails, because an attestation is a statement about a moment and this moment has passed.
cases.name: document-is-older-than-the-freshness-bound

cases.description: A verifier whose clock is behind, or a document from the future. Either way the age is negative and that is reported rather than rounded to zero.
cases.name: now-is-before-the-document-was-produced

cases.description: One bit of the ES384 signature flipped. Everything structural still passes and the signature check fails, which is the only check that can notice.
cases.name: signature-byte-flipped

cases.description: One byte of PCR0 edited inside the signed payload. Two checks fail together: the measurement no longer matches the allowlist, and the signature no longer covers the bytes. PCRs live inside what AWS signed, so they cannot be edited quietly.
cases.name: pcr0-flipped-in-the-payload

cases.description: The document's own timestamp rewritten a year forward — the trick that would make a stale attestation look current. The NSM leaf certificate lives about three hours, so the chain was no longer valid at the moment now claimed, and the signature no longer covers the payload either.
cases.name: timestamp-moved-past-the-certificate-window

cases.description: The last thirty-two bytes cut off. There is no document to reason about, so the format check fails and every other check reports not_implemented by name rather than being silently dropped.
cases.name: truncated-document

cases.description: Arbitrary bytes where a document should be.
cases.name: not-cbor-at-all

cases.description: A debug-mode enclave reports PCR0 as forty-eight zero bytes. Its document is genuine and its signature verifies; the measurements mean nothing because the image was never measured and the parent could read the enclave's memory.
cases.name: debug-enclave-is-refused

cases.description: The same debug document with require_production_mode off, so the two receipt bindings can be seen passing against bytes AWS actually signed: the attested public_key and user_data are exactly what the caller expected.
cases.name: debug-enclave-bindings-match

cases.description: The document vouches for a key, and it is not the key the receipt was signed with. Without this check an attacker could staple any genuine attestation to any receipt.
cases.name: attested-key-is-not-the-receipts-key

cases.description: The enclave was running under a different policy than the receipt claims.
cases.name: attested-user-data-is-not-the-policy-hash

cases.description: A document from eleven months later, signed under a different set of intermediates. It is here so a verifier cannot pass by hard-coding one chain.
cases.name: second-chain-verifies-too

description: Verification cases over real AWS Nitro attestation documents. Each case gives the document, the moment to pin, what the verifier trusted, and the status every named check must report. A second implementation passes when it reproduces every status, not when it reaches the same boolean.
